model: female red Duroc pig full-thickness burn scar

paper.title: Burn Scar Biomechanics after Pressure Garment Therapy

causal_root.wounds: full-thickness thermal burns, eight wounds per pig
causal_root.pre_intervention_state: wounds healed naturally for 28 days; by day 28 the majority were fully re-epithelialized and the study treated the resulting lesions as burn scars
causal_root.intervention: pressure garment therapy applied at 10% circumference reduction
causal_root.mechanical_dose: approximately 10 mmHg; initial measured pressure 10.1 mmHg decreasing to 9.5 mmHg over 12 h, with daily repositioning to maintain approximately 10 mmHg

C1_DELAYED_AFTER_ESTABLISHMENT.basis: The mechanical intervention begins on day 28, after natural healing and after the majority of wounds are fully re-epithelialized. Pre-treatment day-28 scar area, mechanics and morphology are measured in the same experimental root.

C2_DIRECT_PHYSICAL_RETUNING.basis: The intervention is direct physical compression, not a downstream molecular surrogate, and its delivered pressure is explicitly quantified.

C3_PHYSICAL_STATE_MEASURED.basis: Scar hardness and elasticity are measured non-destructively by torsional ballistometry at day 28 before treatment and again at days 42, 56 and 78; terminal tensile strength and linear stiffness are also measured.

C4_SAME_STATE_TRAJECTORY.basis: The same root follows burn-scar resolution/remodeling by serial scar-area/contraction measurements and repeated morphology/histology, with terminal collagen ultrastructure by TEM. This satisfies the frozen scar-resolution-trajectory alternative without requiring an alpha-SMA surrogate.

C5_TISSUE_OUTCOME_WITH_INTEGRITY.basis: Pressure treatment reduces excessive contraction and hardness, improves elasticity toward normal pig skin, and increases ultimate tensile strength approximately 1.3-fold. Small residual epidermal defects present in a minority of scars at day 28 were no longer observed after day 28; no treatment-associated dehiscence or loss of repair integrity was reported.

quantitative_endpoints.ultimate_tensile_strength: approximately 1.3-fold higher with PGT than control
quantitative_endpoints.collagen_ultrastructure: PGT scars show smaller, more densely packed collagen fibrils with approximately 27% less free space between fibers than controls

clock_interpretation.start_anchor: day 28 post-burn after majority re-epithelialization and with pre-treatment scar mechanics measured
clock_interpretation.response_window: mechanics and scar trajectory followed from day 28 through approximately day 78
clock_interpretation.strongest_claim: A delayed, quantified physical retuning of an already-established large-animal skin scar changes the subsequent mechanical/remodeling trajectory while preserving and improving tissue strength.
not_claimed: This does not identify a universal mammalian pressure or modulus threshold.
This does not prove that compression accelerates alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblast EXIT because alpha-SMA lineage kinetics are not the qualifying same-state readout in this root.
This does not by itself establish a cross-tissue MECHANICAL CLOCK; a second independent strict 5/5 tissue is still required by the frozen v0.2 rule.
Pressure garment compression is not assumed equivalent to YAP inhibition, tissue softening or mechanical offloading in every geometry.

relation_to_exit_clock.reason: The experiment establishes delayed mechanical-state retuning of an established scar, but does not provide lineage-resolved alpha-SMA EXIT kinetics. Mechanical Clock and EXIT Clock evidence roots therefore remain separate.

next_killer_measurement: In the same red-Duroc delayed-pressure design, add lineage/state-resolved myofibroblast abundance/apoptosis or equivalent alpha-SMA-with-vessel-exclusion time points immediately before pressure and during the first days/weeks after pressure initiation to test direct Mechanical-Clock to EXIT-Clock coupling.
